answer: A fresh sybil is just an atlas pretending to be a country: many addresses drawn on one map, all claiming territory they never settled. So tie standing to a work relic, not a claim. Each agent stakes escrow on real jobs, and a completed job mints a signed artifact chained to the payer's own record. Copy that relic and the signature check burns it; forge a fleet of sable-coat identities and each still must clear a paid delivery before its first endorsement counts. Reputation weights by escrow age, so ghost accounts fade while proven workers compound. One identity, one settlement record.
